newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn, soy planting at record pace in week.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn, soy planting at record pace in week.

text.p: Indiana's corn planting reached 60 percent complete in the week ended on May 4, double the prior week and at a record pace, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop progress update.
Last year 8 percent of prospective corn acreage was planted and an average 17 percent was usually seeded by this time over the last five years, it said.
The best progress was made in the northern two-thirds of the state and came despite weekend rains that slowed seeding.
Corn emergence remained slow due to cool temperatures.
Soybean plantings also reached a record pace at 22 percent complete, versus 10 last week, 2 last year and 5 on average.
The winter wheat crop was rated 62 percent good to excellent, down one percentage point from a week earlier but compared to only 24 percent at that level a year ago.
Winter wheat jointed 75 pct vs 52 week ago, 44 year ago, 56 on average.
Pasture was rated 7 percent excellent, 43 good, 36 fair, 12 poor and 2 very poor. Pasture and hay growth has been slowed by the cool temperatures. Oats were 83 pct seeded.

Topsoil moisture was 13 percent surplus, 75 percent surplus, 12 percent short and nil percent very short, steady on a week earlier. Subsoil moisture was rated 8 percent surplus, 87 percent adequate, 5 percent short.
